summary: [engine behavior] GF-RUN-2 as claimed (18.1: a group role's commands run through the runner, in a throwaway copy, and a change of the real tree outside the caller's group, .git included, fails the run) does not hold on the managed path. Every role-locked MCP server, a group role's included, still exposes the frozen evidence_run, fix_verify and mutate tools (lib/mcp.js tools() has no per-role filter; install.js lists all of them in the agent's frontmatter), and they run the same plan-pinned commands directly in the real tree with only the frozen integrity window. A backend-engineer test run that way leaves a new file in web/ (frontend's) and commits a change to web/index.html (HEAD moves): status passed, exit 0, nothing detected. An agent is pushed onto that route: the frozen completion refuses the runner's passing evidence as the task's pinned run (its recorded command is the run-check.js wrapper, not the pinned command) and tells the agent to run the command through evidence run instead. (reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ECCode/0d6fc9dd-3a2d-58c2-bf17-c539c4d6f2ed/scratchpad/review-h2/h2-1-evidence-run.test.js)

[engine behavior] 18.4 leaves .eccode/ out of the real-tree hash because 'the frozen record window covers it', and 18.1 (G1-1) says a change through the record's absolute path is put back and fails the run. The frozen record window (lib/evidence.js RECORD_FILES) snapshots only events.jsonl, state.json and config.json. Project code run through gf_run that writes through ECCODE_EVIDENCE to another group's drafts (.eccode/drafts/frontend/), overwrites an evidence log of the record (.eccode/evidence/*.log) or creates .eccode/guards.json (GF-CONF-1: no group role writes it) passes with exit 0; the write is neither put back nor detected nor named in the result. (reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ECCode/0d6fc9dd-3a2d-58c2-bf17-c539c4d6f2ed/scratchpad/review-h2/h2-2-record-dir.test.js)

[engine behavior] GF-CLOSE-6 refuses a valid acceptance by its documented rule. 18.5 lists the refusals exhaustively ('refuses it unless ... the list holds every open finding of the scope exactly once ... and nothing else; and no listed finding is blocking'); closure.acceptanceProblems also refuses an empty list ('a scope with none is closed, not accepted'), which neither 18.5 nor the GF-CLOSE-6 row states. That reason is also wrong: a scope whose readiness no-go stands on the closing tree has no finding at all and cannot close, and the user cannot accept it. Either the rule text or the code must change. (reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ECCode/0d6fc9dd-3a2d-58c2-bf17-c539c4d6f2ed/scratchpad/review-h2/h2-3-accept-empty.test.js)
